RagShortTexts: In 374 AD, Anteans governed from Middle Dnieper & Dniester Forest, under the paramount rule of King Boz.
The polity asserted sovereign legitimacy anchored in Anteans dynastic heritage and royal assemblies.
Surrounded by shifting imperial and tribal pressures, the regime enforced loyalty through binding oaths and martial law.

Variants.Content: In 374 AD, the sovereign authority of Anteans anchored itself within Middle Dnieper & Dniester Forest, confronting the accelerating tremors of Late Antiquity. Governed by King Boz, the state projected imperial legitimacy through dynastic lineage, military patronage, and strict codification of feudal oaths. Emphasizing institutional doctrine rooted in Anteans heritage, the crown mobilized loyal retinues and aristocratic councils to repel external encroachment. Beneath ceremonial grandeur lay unceasing vigilance against shifting steppe incursions and frontier uprisings, compelling the leadership to bind provincial magnates to the throne through land redistribution and martial alliance, safeguarding royal continuity amid an era of continent-wide transition.

Men sworn to King Boz's household gather around the watchfire, retelling the old songs about his victories on the river. The sergeant reminds them that when the war banners are raised, every spear must be ready and every shield must bear the royal sign. The pay they received after the last campaign was fair, and that memory keeps the ranks quiet during the long wait.

The king's steward asks your house to confirm the tributes owed by the river chiefs before the spring assembly. Speak with the chiefs privately and promise to reduce the tribute by one tenth if they swear to the king on the feast day. Keep the reduction off the written tally, since the king's accountants will report any shortfall to the council.
